transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been having some thoughts that scared me. Not that I have a plan to hurt myself, but I’ve caught myself thinking things like… it might be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. That made me feel like I shouldn’t ignore it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yes. Most days I feel low, like there’s this gray film over everything. Even ordinary things, like making tea or looking out at my garden, just feel heavy somehow. I can’t really talk myself out of it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About eight months now, I think. It started after my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly, and it’s just sort of stayed with me since then.
Do you feel these low moods are mainly tied to what’s been happening with your brother?
Yes, I think so. It’s been about eight months, really since his health and behavior changed so suddenly. That’s when I started feeling this way, and it hasn’t really lifted.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. I still get out my watercolor things sometimes, thinking I might paint, but then I just sit there looking at the paper. The enjoyment I used to get from the colors and the light just doesn’t seem to come, so I end up putting it all away.
If your brother’s situation were to improve, do you think your low mood would lift?

I hope it would help, yes. But right now it feels like most days there’s just this gray film over everything. Even simple things, like making tea or looking out at the garden, I still feel this heaviness in me. I can’t quite think my way out of it.
Have these low feelings been there nearly every day for the past eight months?
Yes. Most days it’s there. It’s like a gray film over everything, even when I’m just making tea or looking out at the garden. There’s a heaviness in me that I can’t really talk myself out of.
Before these past eight months, had you already been feeling depressed for at least two years?
No, not for two years. It’s really been about eight months, since my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly.
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to manage your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

Yes, somewhat. I still manage the basics at home and take care of what really has to be done, but I’ve pulled back from things I used to do. I’m not going to my walking group much, and I haven’t been keeping up with mentoring because I just can’t seem to follow through or really be present with people the way I used to.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes. I don’t sleep very well. Some nights I fall asleep all right, other nights it takes a while, but I often wake up around three or four in the morning. Then I start thinking about phone calls I need to make, forms, whether I handled things the right way… and by morning I feel like I barely rested.
Have you been worrying a lot?
I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I do think about things a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call it worrying a lot. It comes and goes.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change, no. My appetite seems about the same, I think.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low in energy?
I don’t think so, not unusually. I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I haven’t noticed a big change in my energy.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I haven’t really noticed trouble concentrating, no. I can usually follow what I’m doing well enough.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yes… not all the time, but I do get stuck feeling like I failed my brother. I keep thinking if I’d been a better sister, or paid closer attention, maybe I would’ve noticed his decline sooner and prevented some of what happened.
Aside from what’s happening with your brother, do you still feel depressed?

Yes. Even apart from my brother, most days things just feel… dimmer. Like there’s a gray film over everything. I can be doing something ordinary, like making tea or looking out at the garden, and there’s still this quiet heaviness in me that I can’t really talk myself out of.
Do you feel your low mood has been stronger than you would expect just from what’s happening with your brother?

Yes, I think so. What’s happening with my brother is part of it, of course, but this feels broader than that. Most days it’s like a gray film over everything, even simple things like making tea or looking out at the garden. There’s just this quiet heaviness that I can’t quite talk myself out of.
Before this period started eight months ago, had you ever gone through another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I’m not sure. I’ve had sad periods before, like anyone, but I don’t know that I’d say I was depressed like this for two weeks or more before this started.
Before these past eight months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Before these past eight months, no, I don’t think so. I’ve had low times, but not that gray-film-over-everything feeling most of the day, nearly every day, like it is now.
Do these feelings seem out of proportion to what most people would be expected to feel in response to your brother’s situation?

Yes, I think it is. I know I’d be upset about my brother, anyone would, but this feels like it’s spread over everything. Most days there’s just this grayness, even when I’m doing ordinary things like making tea or looking at the garden. It feels heavier than I can really explain away.
